quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #4
										  					
  

35 Questions • Passing Score 28

questions.question: If you drive faster than other vehicles on a two-lane road and keep passing cars, you will:

options.text: Get to your destination much faster and safer.
Increase your chance of a crash.
Help reduce traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increase your chance of a crash.
questions.explanation: Avoid passing other vehicles on two-lane roads. Each time you pass a vehicle, your risk of a crash goes up.

questions.question: At a stop sign with no crosswalk, you must stop before entering the intersection.

options.text: True
False

questions.correctAnswerText: True
questions.explanation: At a stop sign, make a complete stop at the stop line if one exists. If there is no stop line, stop before the crosswalk. If there is no crosswalk, stop before entering the intersection.

questions.question: You should be careful when passing large vehicles and avoid driving next to them for long periods.

options.text: TRUE
FALSE

questions.correctAnswerText: TRUE
questions.explanation: Large vehicles have big blind spots on both sides. Do not drive next to a large vehicle for long. It is safer to drop back or move ahead.

questions.question: You cannot pass a school bus when its red lights are flashing.

options.text: True
False

questions.correctAnswerText: True
questions.explanation: When you see a school bus with flashing red lights, stop before you reach it. Stay stopped until the lights turn off. On divided roads, vehicles on the opposite side do not have to stop.

questions.question: If you feel tired while driving, you should:

options.text: Drive faster to reach your destination sooner.
Turn up your radio volume.
Find a safe place to park and take a short nap.

questions.correctAnswerText: Find a safe place to park and take a short nap.
questions.explanation: Watch for signs of fatigue while driving. You are too tired if you struggle to keep your eyes open, drift from your lane, or need the radio loud to stay awake. If this happens, park in a safe place and take a short nap.

questions.question: A pedestrian starts crossing after the "Don't Walk" signal flashes. They are in the middle of the street when your light turns green. You should:

options.text: Go if you have the right-of-way.
Go if the pedestrian is not in your lane.
Wait until the pedestrian finishes crossing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until the pedestrian finishes crossing.
questions.explanation: At a green light, give the right-of-way to any vehicle, bicycle, or pedestrian in the intersection. If a pedestrian begins crossing when the "Don't Walk" signal flashes, wait for them to cross before you go.

questions.question: Temporary signs in construction and work areas have:

options.text: A red background with green writing.
An orange background with black writing.
A yellow background with blue writing.

questions.correctAnswerText: An orange background with black writing.
questions.explanation: All temporary signs in work zones have orange backgrounds with black writing and symbols.

questions.question: When you see a person crossing the street with a white cane or guide dog, you should:

options.text: Stop until they are far away from your path.
Honk your horn as you pass them.
Carefully drive around them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop until they are far away from your path.
questions.explanation: When you see a blind pedestrian using a white cane or guide dog, you must stop until they are well away from your path. Always give them the right-of-way.

questions.question: You should slow down:

options.text: On narrow or winding roads.
At intersections or railroad crossings.
When the road is wet or slippery.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Slow down on narrow or winding roads, near intersections and railroad crossings, on hills, in sharp or blind curves, where there are pedestrians or hazards, and when roads are wet or slippery.

questions.question: A "Merging lanes" sign means you should be ready to change lanes or let other traffic merge into your lane.

options.text: True
False

questions.correctAnswerText: True
questions.explanation: A "Merging lanes" sign means two lanes of traffic going the same direction will soon become one lane. Be ready to change lanes or let other traffic merge into your lane.

questions.question: When turning left at an intersection, what should you do?

options.text: Always yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
Oncoming traffic and pedestrians must yield to you.
Never yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
questions.explanation: When turning left, you must yield to oncoming traffic traveling straight. You must always yield to pedestrians.

questions.question: A pedestrian is crossing illegally in the middle of the street instead of at a crosswalk. You:

options.text: Must stop for them.
Do not have to stop for them.
Should honk your horn at them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must stop for them.
questions.explanation: You must always yield to pedestrians, even if they are jaywalking or crossing where they should not be. Stop for them no matter what.

questions.question: Why should you not make sudden stops in front of large trucks and buses?

options.text: Small vehicle drivers cannot see large trucks and buses well in their rearview mirrors.
Large trucks and buses need longer distances to stop because of their size and weight.
Large trucks and buses travel faster than small vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Large trucks and buses need longer distances to stop because of their size and weight.
questions.explanation: Large vehicles need more time and distance to stop than smaller vehicles. A sudden stop in front of a large vehicle may cause a collision because the driver cannot stop in time.

questions.question: When changing lanes on a highway, you should:

options.text: Signal your lane change.
Check your rearview and outside mirrors.
Check your blind spot by looking over your shoulder.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Always signal before changing lanes. Check your mirrors and look over your shoulder to check your blind spot before moving.

questions.question: When driving in work zones, you should:

options.text: Follow the driver in front of you closely.
Pass the driver in front of you as soon as you can.
Keep a safe distance and do not tailgate.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep a safe distance and do not tailgate.
questions.explanation: In work zones, keep a safe distance from barriers, trucks, equipment, workers, and other vehicles. Increase your following distance and never tailgate.

questions.question: You should always signal when:

options.text: Changing lanes.
Pulling into or out of a parking space.
Pulling into traffic from an alley or parking area.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Always use your turn signal when changing lanes, pulling into or out of a parking space, or pulling into traffic from an alley or parking area. Signals help other drivers know your intentions and prevent accidents.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Sharp turn ahead, slow down.
Work crew ahead.
Side road.
Playground ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Sharp turn ahead, slow down.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They alert drivers to upcoming road conditions and hazards. This sign warns you of a sharp turn ahead. Slow down when you see it.

questions.question: A driving distraction is:

options.text: Anything that causes evasive action while driving.
Anything that takes your attention away from driving.
Anything that causes you to pay more attention to driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Anything that takes your attention away from driving.
questions.explanation: A distraction is anything that pulls your attention away from driving. Distractions can happen anywhere, anytime. They can cause accidents, injuries, and death.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Reduce your speed when the pavement is wet.
The road ahead has a series of turns and curves.
Traffic increases ahead.
Steep grade ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Reduce your speed when the pavement is wet.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that pavement is slippery when wet. Slow down, avoid sudden braking or turning, and increase the distance between your vehicle and the one ahead.

questions.question: When driving in fog, what headlights should you use?

options.text: High beam headlights.
Low beam headlights.
Four-way flashers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in fog, rain, or snow. High beams reflect off these conditions and make visibility worse.

questions.question: Only vehicles with special disability plates or placards may park in spaces marked for people with disabilities.

options.text: True
False

questions.correctAnswerText: True
questions.explanation: A parking space marked for people with disabilities can only be used by vehicles that display disability license plates or disabled parking placards.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Slippery when wet.
Watch for drunk drivers.
Dangerous curve ahead.
Bump in the road ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slippery when wet.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are diamond-shaped with black markings on a yellow background. This sign warns drivers that wet pavement may be slippery, which makes it harder to control your vehicle.

questions.question: Night driving is difficult because:

options.text: The speed limit is higher at night.
There are fewer cars on the roads at night.
It is hard to judge how far away other vehicles are and how fast they are going in the dark.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is hard to judge how far away other vehicles are and how fast they are going in the dark.
questions.explanation: At night, reduced visibility makes it difficult to judge distance and the speed of other vehicles. Your headlights only let you see a limited distance ahead.

questions.question: When you see a green traffic light, you should:

options.text: Continue driving, unless there are vehicles or pedestrians already in the intersection.
Stop if a police officer is nearby.
Treat the intersection like a four-way stop.
Come to a complete stop before proceeding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Continue driving, unless there are vehicles or pedestrians already in the intersection.
questions.explanation: At a green light, yield to pedestrians in the crosswalk and to any vehicles still in the intersection. You may proceed, but be ready to slow down or stop if the light changes before you reach it.

questions.question: When you turn or change lanes, you must:

options.text: Always signal, even if no other traffic is visible.
Signal only if other traffic is visible.
Signal only at night.
Signal only in heavy traffic at night.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always signal, even if no other traffic is visible.
questions.explanation: Always signal when turning, changing lanes, or pulling away from a curb. Make this a habit, even when you don't see other traffic.

questions.question: You must stop your vehicle:

options.text: When a police officer orders you to stop.
At a red traffic light.
Both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: You must come to a complete stop at a red light. You must also always obey instructions from police officers directing traffic, regardless of posted signs or traffic signals.

questions.question: What does alcohol do to your driving ability and judgment?

options.text: It helps driving ability but harms judgment.
It harms both driving ability and judgment.
It has no effect on either.
It harms driving ability but not judgment.

questions.correctAnswerText: It harms both driving ability and judgment.
questions.explanation: Alcohol slows your reaction time and hurts your vision. It also affects your judgment about speed and distance, lowers your caution, and makes you more likely to take risks.

questions.question: Before driving after taking medicine, you should:

options.text: Ask your doctor how it will affect your driving.
Have someone follow you home.
Keep your window open and drive more slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ask your doctor how it will affect your driving.
questions.explanation: Prescription and over-the-counter medicines can impair your driving. Talk to your doctor or pharmacist about how any medicine may affect your driving ability. This is especially important for tranquilizers and sedatives.

questions.question: To safely cross railroad tracks, you should:

options.text: Look both ways, but only when the red light is flashing.
Listen, look both ways, and cross only if it is safe.
Cross quickly when a train is approaching.
Quickly pass under any lowering gates.

questions.correctAnswerText: Listen, look both ways, and cross only if it is safe.
questions.explanation: Railroad crossings are dangerous. Look and listen for trains coming from either direction before crossing. Watch for warning signals and never cross until you are sure it is safe.

questions.question: Under Iowa's Implied Consent Law:

options.text: A police officer can ask you to take a test to measure alcohol in your blood if you are arrested.
Refusing to take the test means your driving license can be taken away.
Both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: Under Iowa's Implied Consent Law, a police officer can ask you to take a breath, urine, or blood test if they think you may be driving under the influence. If you fail the test or refuse to take it, your license can be taken away immediately.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: A left curve is ahead.
A series of curves is ahead.
An S-curve is ahead.
The road will be slippery when wet.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road will be slippery when wet.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that the road is especially slippery when it is wet.

questions.question: Which statement is true?

options.text: Sudden weather changes require you to change how you drive.
You should slow down when driving in rain and fog.
Watch for vehicles coming up behind you in bad weather.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: When weather changes suddenly, adjust your driving. Slow down in rain and fog. Watch for vehicles behind you that may be going too fast.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: No right turn.
Curve.
Turn right or left.
Traffic flows only in the direction of the arrow.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic flows only in the direction of the arrow.
questions.explanation: This one-way sign shows that traffic moves only in the direction the arrow points.

questions.question: What should you do to drive safely at night?

options.text: Increase your following distance.
Do not drive if you are tired.
Make sure your headlights work properly.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: At night, you cannot see as well. Take these steps to stay safe and help other drivers stay safe.

questions.question: When an emergency vehicle with sirens and flashing lights approaches, the driver should pull to the right edge of the road and wait for it to pass.

options.text: True
False

questions.correctAnswerText: True
questions.explanation: When an emergency vehicle with lights and/or sirens approaches, pull to the right side of the road right away and let it pass.
